source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary (Business Standard): Divi's plays a China+1 strategy for major pharma companies as they look to de-leverage from dependence on Chinese API manufacturers, citing Divi's cost leadership, existing capacity and regulatory track record. Not a direct AR quote — third-party attribution.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported near debt-free (debt/equity ~0) across recent years; no floating-rate liability disclosure found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Search snippets reference solvent recovery/backward integration reducing input-cost exposure, but no explicit crude-oil-linked raw material % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~90% of sales per third-party synthesis (Europe+US combined ~74% of total revenue); currency-specific (USD) breakdown and hedging policy not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: One source places Divi's in the broader Category-2 API/KSM applicant pool for the PLI-Bulk Drugs scheme, but no confirmation of approved-beneficiary status or incentive receipt was found.

rural.evidence: News/earnings commentary: rural demand remains healthy, supported by improved rural demand and financing availability, cited as a tailwind for Royal Enfield's two-wheeler volumes — no revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Re: VE Commercial Vehicles (54.4%-owned CV JV, consolidated): healthy YoY growth supported by the Government's continued push on infrastructure spending, demand from mining and construction activities (ICRA rating rationale) — no % of consolidated revenue disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors reported effectively debt-free with strong net cash; no floating-rate liability disclosure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield FY25 exports reached ~100,136 of ~1,002,893 total units (~10%, up 29.7% YoY), supported by new Bangladesh/Nepal assembly facilities — unit-based proxy, not a revenue-currency disclosure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors was among 20 companies approved under the PLI 'Champion OEM Incentive Scheme' for Automobile & Auto Components (approved Feb 2022, per PIB release); no incentive revenue % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Management quoted (via IPO coverage): Anthem is positioned as 'the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones,' with cost arbitrage cited as driving capacity expansion as a China alternative for global pharma/biotech clients.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Reported net-cash balance sheet (~Rs 465-625 Cr net cash across recent quarters, debt/equity ~0.05x); no floating-rate liability % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Analyst commentary: margins remain vulnerable to FX fluctuations with export markets accounting for about 75-80% of revenues, serving 550+ clients across 44-50 countries — no specific hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found confirming Anthem Biosciences (biologics/enzymes/peptides CRDMO) is an approved beneficiary under the PLI-Bulk Drugs or PLI-Pharma schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sector/analyst commentary: government capex push, PLI schemes, and China+1 manufacturing shifts are lifting industrial orders across drives, motors, process automation, and low-voltage products for ABB India; ABB India's own reporting emphasizes a 'local for local' manufacturing strategy across 10 India factories. No explicit first-person China+1 framing found in AR text itself.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India saw strong traction from government-backed sectors such as transportation, manufacturing, data centers, electrification, renewables, and digitalization; National Electricity Plan/PGCIL capex implies ~Rs 5-6 lakh crore incremental T&D capex over CY26-CY30, of which 20-25% flows to electrification products ABB supplies. No % of ABB revenue tied to government capex disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India reported near debt-free with ~Rs 51.9 billion net cash (Jun 2025); no floating-rate liability % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Commodity and forex hedging used to partly offset currency losses (per Q4 results commentary); detailed policy not confirmed from primary source.
inr_exposure.evidence: ABB India's forex loss in Q4 was largely offset by commodity hedging and efficiency gains; higher import content in raw material cited as a near-term margin headwind — no revenue-currency % disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that ABB India itself is an approved PLI scheme beneficiary; PLI referenced only as an industry/customer-side tailwind driving orders.

inr_exposure.evidence: International formulations (Russia, South Africa, US, branded generics exports) plus CDMO/API together were ~42% of FY25 revenue (Domestic Rs2,269cr; International Rs1,128cr; CDMO Rs446cr; API Rs76cr of Rs3,918cr total) — implies material multi-currency (RUB, ZAR, USD) exposure, though no consolidated USD% or hedging policy was disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin management commentary: well-positioned to support global pharma players' efforts to diversify suppliers away from China, leveraging India-based manufacturing and CDMO operations (API Plus and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions). ~25% of materials imported with some China dependence being actively calibrated via alternate India-based suppliers (per search summaries, not verified against primary MD&A text).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Per financial-instruments risk disclosure (secondary summary): floating rate debt target set at a maximum of 30% of total debt outstanding — a policy ceiling, not necessarily the realized mix; not independently verified against primary AR text.

inr_exposure.evidence: US business (largely USD-denominated) was ~36-38% of FY25 global sales (USD 925mn); geographic mix reported as US 36%, India 34%, RoW 24%, API 5%. No specific FX hedging policy text located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Public list of companies qualified under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals includes Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr Reddy's, Glenmark, Wockhardt, Biocon, Aurobindo, Intas, Natco and Lupin (55 companies qualified); specific revenue impact not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/broker commentary: rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits Navin Fluorine's export-led business; company built backward integration via a 25% JV with India's only fluorspar beneficiation company specifically to diversify raw-material sourcing away from China. Third-party sourced; not verified against primary MD&A text.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw material is fluorspar (not crude oil) — China dominates global supply in fluorspar (40%+ of raw material costs); Navin has signed long-term supply contracts with South African miners and holds a fluorspar-beneficiation JV to de-risk this exposure. No crude-oil-specific input cost disclosure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution cited at ~66.6% (full-year) and ~77% in Q4FY25, implying substantial foreign-currency revenue; no consolidated USD% or hedging policy text located.

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI scheme for agrochemicals/specialty chemicals was reported as being finalized by the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, but no source confirmed Navin Fluorine as an approved beneficiary as of the FY24-25 report.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forward-contract hedging of trade receivables in major currencies (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, JPY)
inr_exposure.evidence: OFSS Annual Report 2023-24, Notes to Financial Statements: 'The OFSS group manages its foreign currency risk by hedging the receivables in the major currencies (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP and JPY) using hedging instrument as forward contracts... As of balance sheet date, the OFSS group's net foreign currency exposure expressed in INR that is not hedged is Rs 2,630.44 million.' Geographic segment revenue (FY24): India 9.6%, United States 28.1%, Rest of Americas 8.1%, Europe 14.6%, Asia Pacific 21.1%, Middle East & Africa 18.5% of consolidated revenue of Rs 63,729.61 million.

govt_capex.evidence: NOTE: BSE 509496 / CEMPRO is not a cement manufacturer — it is Cemindia Projects Ltd, formerly ITD Cementation India Ltd, an EPC/infrastructure construction company (marine, MRTS, airports, highways), renamed Aug/Sep 2025 after acquisition by Renew Exim (Adani-linked) from Italian-Thai Development. Order book composition reported ~45% Government and ~20% PSU clients (FY23 disclosure, most recent found); works for state/central government departments, ministries, municipal bodies across MRTS, airports, ports, highways, irrigation. This is order-book mix, not revenue mix, and not from the most recent FY24-25 AR directly.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Reported net debt-to-equity of ~0.30x as of Q1 FY25 (brokerage note); no floating-rate liability % disclosed in sources available.

crude_exposure.evidence: EPC/construction operations exposed to bitumen, steel, cement, diesel and fuel cost inflation (industry-wide commentary); no company-specific raw material % of revenue found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company described as operating in India only; no export revenue or forex disclosure found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company targets raising export share from ~3% to 10% (longer-term 15-20% by 2030) per Autocar Professional coverage; FY24 AR separately notes Make in India/PLI positioning India's manufacturing sector to become a USD 1-trillion industry by FY2025-26 — general macro tailwind commentary, not an explicit China+1/diversification-driven order-growth narrative.

rural.evidence: 62% of Gabriel's total sales come from the two-and-three-wheeler segment (incl. aftermarket); rural areas account for ~55% of national two-wheeler sales (industry-wide figure), implying meaningful indirect rural linkage, but no company-specific rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company faces raw material price volatility from steel, aluminum, and rubber (a crude-derivative input); no specific % of revenue or COGS disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were Rs 34 crore, ~3% of FY2024-25 revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Gabriel India does not appear on lists of PLI-Auto (Component Champion) approved beneficiaries found (e.g. Maruti, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Motherson, Bosch, Lucas-TVS); FY24 AR references PLI/Make in India only as a sector-level tailwind, not as a scheme Gabriel directly participates in.

inr_exposure.evidence: US business contributed ~19.1% of overall sales (Rs 634 crore) in Q3 FY25; other international markets (Latin America, Australia, Europe combined) contributed ~9.8% (Rs 326.5 crore); India sales ~71.1% of total.

pli_scheme.evidence: Third-party sources note Alkem as a leading global cephalosporin API manufacturer, relevant to India's PLI-for-APIs/bulk-drug-park push, but no confirmation found that Alkem itself is an approved PLI scheme beneficiary or receives PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party industry analysis (not the AR itself): geopolitical friction between the West and China has accelerated the China Plus One sourcing strategy, benefiting Indian exporters, with companies like Sun Pharma leveraging their portfolios. No direct AR quote explicitly framing revenue/order growth as China+1-driven was located.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company reported to use derivative financial instruments (forwards/options/swaps) and hedge accounting for currency exposure; currencies other than USD translated to USD at period-end rates for reporting purposes (general description, not a direct FY25 AR quote).
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 sales composition: India Formulations 33%, US Formulations 31%, Emerging Markets Formulations 18%, Rest of World Formulations 14%, API & Others 4% (total sales Rs 520 billion).

china_plus_one.evidence: AR (Risk Mitigation): 'Amid geopolitical instability and global trade restrictions, including the Red Sea crisis that threatened global supply chains, the Company swiftly activated contingency plans...It diversified sourcing and logistics strategies, established alternative shipping routes.' Company operates 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, USA, Mexico and China; no explicit 'China+1' term or revenue attribution used.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Notes to financial statements (Interest rate risk exposure): Variable rate borrowings INR 134.63 million vs. Fixed rate borrowings INR Nil as at 31st March 2025 — i.e. 100% of the Company's/Group's borrowings are variable/floating rate.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved currency hedging policy primarily using forward contracts
inr_exposure.evidence: 'The Company carries out currency hedging based upon a Board approved hedging policy which primarily employs forward contracts as a medium of hedging its currency risk.' Also: 'Fluctuations in commodity prices can significantly affect the Company's manufacturing costs...it is not always possible to fully predict, hedge, or offset the impact of price volatility.'

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review: 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.' Also acquired Railway Equipment Division and produces motors for electric two-wheelers under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry from the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A (Industry Review): 'By FY 2027-28, the Indian auto component industry plans to invest USD 7 billion to boost the localisation of advanced components such as electric motors and automatic transmissions. This initiative aims to reduce import reliance and capitalise on the China+1 strategy.' Framed as industry-level opportunity, not directly attributed to Endurance's own revenue growth.

rural.evidence: MD&A (Two-wheeler segment): 'With sales of 23.81 million units in FY 2024-25, two-wheelers market witnessed a growth of 11.1%...This growth can be attributed to improved rural demand and revival of consumer confidence...driven by improved rural and semi-urban connectivity.' No company-specific rural revenue % disclosed; Endurance is a Tier-1 supplier heavily linked to 2W OEMs.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Notes (Interest rate risk): 'The Group's exposure to the risk of changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Group's debt obligations which have floating rate indebtedness.' Non-current borrowings interest rates range from Euribor 3-month to 6-month with spread 0.002%-2.200% p.a. No explicit fixed/floating % split table disclosed (unlike Sona).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved Forex Risk Management Policy; forward contracts used to hedge transactional FX exposure, but long-term investment in subsidiaries (Endurance Overseas SpA, Italy) left unhedged
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Wherever transactions are undertaken in foreign currency, the Group hedges the risk of foreign exchange fluctuation by using derivative financial instruments in line with its risk management policies. The investment in subsidiaries being long term in nature is unhedged.' Group exposed to EUR, USD, CHF, CNY, GBP, SGD, JPY.

pli_scheme.evidence: MD&A only references PLI at the macro/industry level ('While the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) strengthened various sectors in the economy...') — no statement that Endurance itself is a PLI scheme beneficiary or recipient of PLI-linked income.

rural.evidence: BRSR/Corporate governance disclosures note desired director experience 'in developing strategies to grow sales and market shares in semi-urban and rural markets'; CSR sections reference rural livelihood/craft programmes (e.g. Project Tarasha). No quantified rural revenue % disclosed for Titan/Tanishq.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Short-term unsecured borrowings (tenure 7-90 days) at market-linked rates of 6.99%-9.15% p.a., commercial paper, and 'Gold on loan' scheme payable to banks (interest 1.50%-5.50% p.a.) reprice frequently but AR does not present an explicit fixed-vs-floating % breakdown.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forward foreign exchange contracts and option contracts used to mitigate FX risk on normal purchase/sale transactions; gold-related FX risk managed separately
inr_exposure.evidence: 'The Group is exposed to foreign exchange risk arising through its sales and purchases denominated in various foreign currencies...the Group enters into forward foreign exchange contracts and option contracts to mitigate the risk of changes in exchange rates...mainly exposed to USD, CHF, EURO, SGD, AED, JPY, HKD, CAD, AUD and GBP currencies.' Exports are only 2.68% of turnover, limiting overall INR exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage indicates Shyam Metalics is a beneficiary of anti-dumping duty on aluminium foil imports from China, but this is an import-protection dynamic, not a supply-chain diversification/China+1 narrative attributed to revenue growth. No AR text located.

govt_capex.evidence: Per third-party summary of FY25 management commentary: demand continues to be supported by broad-based strength across major steel consuming sectors, including infrastructure-led construction activity, manufacturing activity, urbanization, with spending on huge infra projects such as road, railways, power (source: earnings-call/press summary, not directly verified against primary AR text).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial summaries indicate total debt of approx. INR 10.9 billion against equity of ~INR 118.6 billion (low leverage, debt-to-equity ~9-10%), suggesting limited overall rate sensitivity, but no primary-source floating-rate disclosure was accessible.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company has commissioned an aluminium foil facility (Odisha, ~INR 800 crore investment, commercial production reported in 2026) targeting battery-grade foil for lithium-ion cell/ACC manufacturing, positioning it as a supplier into India's PLI-linked ACC ecosystem — but this is downstream of the FY2024-25 reporting period and does not establish Shyam Metalics itself as a direct PLI scheme beneficiary in the FY2024-25 AR.

rural.evidence: Analyst commentary paraphrasing MD&A: consumption in Tier-2/3/4 cities and rural areas could outpace urban cities, which USL is positioned to capture via its well-entrenched manufacturing and distribution footprint across India, though strict advertising rules for alcohol limit rural penetration (via ICICIdirect/HDFC Sec research notes citing USL commentary).

inr_exposure.evidence: Multiple sources (equitymaster AR analyses, financial press) repeat that India accounts for 99.6% of net sales for United Spirits, exporting to over 37 countries but with minimal international revenue contribution, implying limited direct FX/USD revenue exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: From Sai Life Q3 FY25 earnings-call commentary (via secondary summary): management stated pharma 'has made a long-term decision to diversify from China' with a 5-10 year horizon, and noted molecules shifting from China to India, with a fairly large tranche occurring around the 2023-2024 timeframe — explicitly framing China+1 as a driver of order/revenue growth for the CRDMO business.

rate_sensitive.evidence: General risk-factor language (via secondary summary of AR/financial notes): the company uses derivative financial instruments or other hedging techniques to cover potential exposure to foreign currency and interest rate fluctuations — no specific floating-rate liability percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedging supplemented by derivative instruments, described in secondary summaries as imperfect — almost all revenue is in USD/EUR while costs are in INR; a strong rupee hurts margins.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributing up to 97-99% of total revenues, primarily driven by companies in the United States and Europe, with revenue overwhelmingly USD/EUR denominated against an INR cost base (via analyst/secondary summaries, not directly verified against AR text).

rural.evidence: Analyst initiating-coverage note (Axis Direct/Simplywall.st, paraphrasing company disclosures): Rainbow added 280 beds in FY24 (highest-ever annual addition at the time) via new spoke hospitals in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai, and is entering its next leg of growth through greenfield projects including tier-2/3 expansion (e.g. Coimbatore hub hospital, ~130 beds) as part of a plan to add 2,500+ beds over five years.

govt_capex.evidence: Analyst commentary (Marcellus 'Little Champs' newsletter, paraphrasing management/AR disclosure): Rainbow has no meaningful exposure to government or institutional schemes such as Ayushman Bharat, maintaining a roughly 50:50 insurance-to-cash payer mix and renegotiating TPA rates every two years to protect margins — i.e. deliberately low government-scheme revenue exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Secondary financial-data summaries indicate Rainbow operates with zero long-term debt, having fully repaid its borrowings by March 2024, with planned Rs 950-1,000 crore capex over three years to be entirely funded through internal accruals — implying minimal floating-rate liability exposure, though no AR-disclosed percentage was found.

rural.evidence: Company/analyst description (via BlinkX/AlphaStreet summaries of Radico's positioning): vertically integrated approach encompassing grain-to-bottle manufacturing, with a pan-India sales network reaching over 60,000 retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst/secondary AR-summary commentary: ENA and packaging materials are two key raw-material components; during FY2024 the cost of grain, ENA, and glass was volatile, leading to significant pressure on gross margins, and the company has been shifting from glass to PET bottles in the regular segment — indicating indirect petrochemical/packaging cost linkage, but no explicit crude-oil percentage was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico is described as one of the leading exporters of Beverage Alcohol from India, available in over 85 countries spanning 6 continents including Travel Retail, with international brands (e.g. Rampur Single Malt, Jaisalmer Gin) exclusive to export markets; international/exports business expected to cross Rs 500 Cr net sales mark in FY26 — but no export revenue percentage of total sales was found.
